subject: ss-nephrology
title: Renal physiology: filtration, feedback and tubular handling of sodium

steps.tx: The **glomerular filtration rate** (GFR) is the volume of plasma filtered per minute across the glomerular capillaries. Filtration is driven by Starling forces: capillary hydrostatic pressure favours filtration, while capillary oncotic pressure and Bowman space hydrostatic pressure oppose it. Filtration is restricted by size and by charge, the negatively charged glomerular basement membrane repelling anionic proteins such as albumin. In healthy adults the glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure is about 55 mm Hg, which is the main driving force.

steps.tx: Renal blood flow is kept steady by **autoregulation**. The **myogenic response** is an intrinsic reaction of the afferent arteriole to stretch. The **tubuloglomerular feedback** (TGF) works through the macula densa, which senses sodium chloride delivered to the thick ascending limb. High delivery constricts the afferent arteriole and lowers GFR. Loop diuretics block NKCC2 and therefore blunt this feedback, a point often tested in exams.

Tubuloglomerular feedback works through the macula densa, which senses sodium chloride delivered to the thick ascending limb. High delivery constricts the afferent arteriole and lowers the glomerular filtration rate. Loop diuretics block the NKCC2 transporter and therefore blunt this feedback, a point often tested in exams.

steps.tx: The **renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system** (RAAS) starts when juxtaglomerular cells release renin in response to low renal perfusion pressure, macula densa signalling and sympathetic beta-1 stimulation. Renin cleaves angiotensinogen to angiotensin I. **ACE** removes two C-terminal amino acids to form angiotensin II. Angiotensin II constricts the efferent arteriole, stimulates aldosterone, and acts centrally to raise sympathetic drive. Circulating renin has a half-life of about 10 to 15 minutes.

steps.tx: **Aldosterone** acts on principal cells of the collecting duct. It raises the apical abundance of the epithelial sodium channel (**ENaC**) and the basolateral Na/K ATPase, so sodium is retained and potassium is lost. In primary hyperaldosteronism, aldosterone is autonomous, so renin is suppressed. Resistant hypertension, defined as poor control on three drugs including a diuretic, is a formal indication to screen for primary hyperaldosteronism.

steps.tx: The **countercurrent multiplier** builds the medullary osmotic gradient. The thick ascending limb pumps out sodium, potassium and chloride through NKCC2, leaving the interstitium hypertonic while the fluid stays dilute. The descending limb is permeable to water through aquaporins, allowing concentration. NCC in the distal convoluted tubule handles thiazide-sensitive sodium reabsorption. Proximal tubule reabsorbs about 65 percent of filtered sodium and water.

steps.tx: Renal clearance quantifies handling. Clearance equals urine concentration times urine flow divided by plasma concentration. **Fractional excretion** compares the clearance of a solute with that of creatinine, and a clearance ratio above 1 against inulin signals net secretion. Creatinine is a practical GFR marker because it is produced steadily but is slightly secreted. Free water clearance estimates the excess water excreted beyond osmolar clearance, guiding dilution and concentration.
